quotes.text:
One problem with both Android, and Ios: impossible to disable automatic previews

Send yourself a link by SMS, or some popular messenger like Whatsapp.

Your phone will automatically make you a browser page preview, and in the process run every browser exploit available.

Google added an extremely well hidden option to disable it it Messages few versions ago. Since there is no way to be sure Google does not remove it, and add some kind of another autoplay like feature in the future, I just replaced the SMS app altogether to one which does not peek into my conversations https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.simplemobiletools.smsmessenger (google straight tells they can get a copy of your SMSes as per their disclaimer if you use Google Messages for "improving service")

I have mixed feelings about this, and especially about the google application: it's nearly 300MB.

In comparison, Conversations, which is a full-fledged XMPP client with voice and video included, is ~70MB.

Beyond this, any use of the google app comes with lengthy Terms & Conditions, which is not something I really want in my SMS application.

I moved to Simple SMS Messenger[^1], which doesn't support anything beyond basic SMS & MMS, but it's small, fast, and open source.

[^1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.simplemobiletools.smsmessenger
